Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:1:1.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan wondered about it - About this [statement] of Rabbi Oshaya:

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:1:2.hebrew: וכי אומרים לו לאדם כו' - דכל בהמות מזבח אסור לחללה תמימה, שנאמר: "אם בבהמה הטמאה ופדה בערכך", ואמר מר (מנחות דף קא.): "בבעלי מומין שנפדו הכתוב מדבר, יכול יופדו על מום עובר כו'". וזה שבא לימלך ולחוב בדמיה, נאמר לו: "עמוד וחטא לחללה מזיד, בשביל שתזכה לתקן הקרבתה של בהמה זו":
Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:1:2.english: And does one say to a person, etc. - For [with regard to] any animal [designated for] the altar, it is forbidden to desacralize it [while it is] unblemished, as it is stated: "And if it be of an unclean animal, then he shall redeem it according to your valuation" (Leviticus 27:27); and the Master said (Menachot 101a): "Scripture speaks of blemished animals that are redeemed; could [one think] they may be redeemed on account of a temporary blemish, etc.?" And [as for] this [person] who comes to consult [the court] and to obligate himself for its value, shall we say to him: "Arise and sin by desacralizing it intentionally, in order that you may merit to rectify the sacrifice of this animal"?

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:1:3.hebrew: אלא אמר רבי יוחנן - הא דקתני ״זכרים עולות״ — לא היא ולא דמיה קריבין בעודה תמימה, אלא ממתין לה עד שתומם מום קבוע, ויהא מותר לחללה. ומייתי שתי בהמות: חדא לעולה וחדא לשלמים, ומתנה: אם זו עולה — תהא זו עולה תחתיה, וחבירתה שלמי נדבה; ואם זו שלמים — תהא זו שלמים תחתיה, וחבירתה עולת נדבה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:1:3.english: Rather, Rabbi Yoḥanan says - That which [the Mishnah] taught, [that] males [are] burnt-offerings — neither it nor its value is offered while it is unblemished; rather, he waits for it until it develops a permanent blemish, and it will be permitted to desacralize it. And he brings two animals, one for a burnt-offering and one for a peace-offering, and stipulates: If this [found animal] is a burnt-offering, let this [one] be a burnt-offering in its stead, and its fellow a voluntary peace-offering; and if this [found animal] is a peace-offering, let this [one] be a peace-offering in its stead, and its fellow a voluntary burnt-offering.

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:2:1.english: That he also brings a thanks-offering - And stipulates.

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:3:1.hebrew: ודילמא אשם הוא - וליכא למימר דנייתי נמי אשם, דאין אשם בא נדבה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:3:1.english: And perhaps it is a guilt-offering - And it cannot be said that he should also bring a guilt-offering [and stipulate], for a guilt-offering is not brought as a freewill offering.

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:3:2.hebrew: ומשני אשם בן שתי שנים - דאשם גזילות ומעילות ושפחה חרופה כתיב בהן איל, והאי מתני' דאשתכח בן שנה, וליכא לספוקי באשם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:3:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: A guilt-offering is in its second year - For regarding the guilt-offering for robbery, [the guilt-offering for] misuse of consecrated items, and [the guilt-offering for] a designated maidservant, "a ram" is written concerning them; and this Mishnah [refers to a case] where [the animal] that was found was in its first year, and [so] there is no reason to suspect [that it might be] a guilt-offering.

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:3:3.english: And perhaps [it is] the guilt-offering of a nazirite or the guilt-offering of a leper - For “a lamb” is written regarding them [which is in its first year].

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:4:1.english: In its time - As long as it is fit for a Paschal offering.

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:4:2.english: Not in its time - Its time has passed.

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:4:3.english: It is a peace-offering - And behold, he [already] brings a peace-offering.

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:5:1.hebrew: למאי הלכתא - תירוצא הוא. כלומר: למאי הילכתא אתית לספוקינהו בבכור ומעשר? למיכלינהו במומו — שספק בכור וספק מעשר נאכלין במומן לבעלים, שהרי אין להם פדיון? והני נמי, לכשנפדו, נאכלין במומן, ואוכלן בתורת בכור ומעשר, שאין נשחטין באיטליז ואין נשקלין בליטרא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:5:1.english: With regard to which halakha - This is an answer. That is to say: With regard to which halakha do you come to consider them doubtful as a firstborn or [animal] tithe? [Is it with regard] to eating them in their blemish — as a doubtful firstborn and a doubtful [animal] tithe are eaten in their blemish by the owners, since they have no redemption? These [found animals] as well, when they are redeemed, are eaten in their blemish, and he eats them under the laws of a firstborn and [animal] tithe, [in] that they are not slaughtered in a butcher shop and are not weighed by the pound.

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:7:1.hebrew: חטאת בת שנתה - היא, דכתיב (ויקרא ה׳:ו׳): "נקבה מן הצאן כשבה", וכל כשבה (בן שנה) [בת שנתה] היא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:7:1.english: A sin-offering is in its first year - It is [in its first year], as it is written: “A female from the flock, a ewe-lamb” (Leviticus 5:6), and every ewe-lamb is in its first year.

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:7:2.hebrew: ואישתכח בת שתי שנים - ובהמה דמתניתין, בבת שתי שנים עסקינן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:7:2.english: And an animal in its second year was found - And [as for] the animal of our Mishnah, we are dealing with [one that is] in its second year.

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:8:1.hebrew: עז בת שנתה לחטאת - לישנא דקרא (במדבר ט״ו:כ״ז) לסימנא בעלמא נקט, כלומר: אם בת שנתה היא, מקריבה חטאת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:8:1.english: A goat in its first year as a sin-offering - He merely cited the phrasing of the verse (Numbers 15:27) as an indicator, that is to say: If it is in its first year, he offers it as a sin-offering.

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:8:2.hebrew: חטאת סלקא דעתך - דילמא לאו חטאת היא, והיכי קריבה? ותנאי נמי ליכא, דחטאת לא קרבה נדבה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:8:2.english: Can it enter your mind [that it is brought as] a sin-offering? - Perhaps it is not a sin-offering, and how can it be sacrificed? And there cannot even be a stipulation [made], as a sin-offering is not brought as a voluntary offering:

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:8:3.hebrew: כחטאת כונסה לכיפה והיא מתה מאיליה - כדין חטאת שאינה ראויה ליקרב, כגון חמש חטאות דאזלי למיתה (תמורה דף טז.):
Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:8:3.english: As a sin-offering, he conveys it into a cell and it dies on its own - In accordance with the law of a sin-offering that is not fit to be sacrificed, such as the five sin-offerings that are left to die (Temurah 16a).

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:8:4.hebrew: לכיפה - לאו דוקא, או שמא כיפה היתה מתוקנת לכך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:8:4.english: Into a cell - [This is] not exact; or perhaps a cell was designated for this [purpose].

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:8:5.english: And it dies - For they do not give it food.

Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:9:1.hebrew: אין לוקחין בהמות במעות מעשר שני - חוץ לירושלים, דכתיב (דברים י״ד:כ״ה) "וצרת הכסף בידך", ועוד: שמא תכחיש בטורח הדרך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 55b:9:1.english: One may not purchase animals with second-tithe money - [This means] outside of Jerusalem, as it is written: (Deuteronomy 14:25) “And you shall bind up the money in your hand”; and furthermore, lest [the animal] become emaciated from the toil of the journey.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 55b:2:1.hebrew: דמייתי נמי תודה - וא"ת: ואמאי צריך להביא בהמה אחרת לתודה? באותה עצמה שיעשה זבחי שלמים יתנה ויאמר: "אם אינה שלמים — תהא תודה!" ואי משום המתנות — הוו שוין. ואי משום דלא שוו באכילתן, דשלמים נאכלים לשני ימים ולילה אחד ותודה ליום ולילה, ואין מביאין קדשים לבית הפסול — ע"כ האי תנא קסבר דמביאין, מדקתני בסמוך: "פסח שלא בזמנו — שלמים", ואע"ג דפסח אינו נאכל אלא ליום ולילה ושלמים נאכלים לב' ימים ולילה, אלמא לא חייש מן האכילה! וי"ל: משום דתודה בעי לחם. וא"ת: לייתי לחם ויתנה: "אם היא תודה — הרי לחמה, ואם היא שלמים — תהא הלחם נדבה"? הא אין לחם בא נדבה, וחולין בעזרה הוא, כדאמרינן בפרק התודה (מנחות דף פ:):
Tosafot on Kiddushin 55b:2:1.english: That he also brings a thanks-offering - And if you say: Why does he need to bring another animal for a thanks-offering? With that very one that he makes [his] peace-offering, let him stipulate and say: "If it is not a peace-offering, let it be a thanks-offering!" And if [one would suggest that this cannot be done] because of the applications [of blood] — they are equal. And if [one would suggest that this cannot be done] because they are not equal in their [permissible time for] eating — as peace-offerings are eaten for two days and one night, while a thanks-offering [is eaten only] for a day and a night, and [by doing so] one brings consecrated offerings to the realm of disqualification — perforce this Tanna holds that one may bring [them to the realm of disqualification], since it teaches nearby: "A Paschal offering not in its time is a peace-offering," and even though a Paschal offering is eaten only for a day and a night, whereas peace-offerings are eaten for two days and a night — thus [we see that] he is not concerned about [shortening the time for] eating! And one can say: [He must bring a separate animal] because a thanks-offering requires bread. And if you say: Let him bring bread and stipulate: "If it is a thanks-offering, here is its bread; and if it is a peace-offering, let the bread be a voluntary offering"? — Bread does not come as a voluntary offering, and [bringing it would be bringing] unconsecrated [items] into the Temple Courtyard, as we say in the chapter [entitled] HaToda (Menachot 80b).

Tosafot on Kiddushin 55b:3:1.hebrew: ודילמא אשם הוא - ואם תאמר: ויתנה באותן של שלמים, דהא שוו במתנות? ואי משום סמיכה, דשלמים טעונין סמיכה ואשם אין טעון סמיכה — הא סמיכה לא מעכבא! ואי משום אכילה — הא קסבר דמביאים קדשים לבית הפסול! ויש לומר: דאין להתנות אשם בשלמים, שהרי שלמים טעונין נסכים ואשם אין טעון נסכים. ואין לומר שיתנה לנסכים ויאמר: "אם היא שלמים מוטב, ואם לאו יהו נסכי נדבה" — שהרי אין נסכי חובה ונסכי נדבה שוין, שנסכי חובה לספלים ונסכי נדבה מזלפן על גבי אישים:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 55b:3:1.english: "And perhaps it is a guilt-offering" - And if you say: Let him stipulate with those [animals brought] for peace-offerings, since they are identical in their [blood] applications? And if [you say he cannot do so] because of the laying of hands (semikhah) — as peace-offerings require semikhah and a guilt-offering does not require semikhah — surely semikhah is not indispensable! And if [you say he cannot do so] because of eating — surely he holds that one may bring consecrated items to the place of disqualification! And one can say: One cannot stipulate a guilt-offering with a peace-offering, because a peace-offering requires libations and a guilt-offering does not require libations. And one cannot say that he should make a stipulation regarding the libations and say: "If it is a peace-offering, good, and if not, let them be voluntary libations" — for obligatory libations and voluntary libations are not identical, as obligatory libations [go] to the basins, and voluntary libations, one sprinkles them upon the fire-offerings [on the altar].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 55b:3:2.hebrew: ודילמא אשם נזיר ואשם מצורע הוא - ואם תאמר: אשם מצורע מיהא יתנה בשלמים, שהרי שוין הן בנסכים? ויש לומר: דעיקר קושיא מאשם נזיר, ואשם מצורע נקט אגב אשם נזיר. עוד י"ל: דבאשם מצורע איכא חששא אחרינא, שצריך ליתן מדמו על בהונות מצורע, והכא ליכא מצורע. עוד אמר ה"ר שמשון מקוצי: דאין לומר שיתנה אשם בשלמים, דשמא היום או למחר ידע בעל האשם שנאבד האשם, ויביא אחר תחתיו, ולא ידע שנמצא, ויהיה אותו שיביא חולין לעזרה — משום דהוי אשם שנתכפרו בעליו באחר, (ולמיתה) [ולרעייה] אזלא. והשתא ניחא דלא מצי להקשות מידי. אבל בעולה ליכא למיחש להא אם יביא עולה אחרת, שהרי עולה בא נדבה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 55b:3:2.english: "And perhaps it is the guilt-offering of a nazirite or the guilt-offering of a leper" - And if you should say: The guilt-offering of a leper, at least, let him stipulate with peace-offerings, for they are equivalent in [requiring] libations? Then one can say: The primary question was from the guilt-offering of a nazirite, and [the Gemara] mentioned the guilt-offering of a leper [merely] along with the guilt-offering of a nazirite. Furthermore, one can say: In the case of the guilt-offering of a leper, there is another concern, for [the priest] must place some of its blood upon the thumbs and toes of the leper, and here there is no leper [present]. Furthermore, Rabbi Samson of Coucy said: It cannot be said that he should stipulate [the found animal as] a guilt-offering with peace-offerings, for perhaps today or tomorrow the owner of the guilt-offering will learn that the guilt-offering was lost, and he will bring another in its stead, not knowing that it was found, and that [animal] which he brings will be non-sacred [meat slaughtered] in the Temple courtyard — because it is a guilt-offering whose owner has achieved atonement through another, which goes (to die) [to pasture]. And now [according to Rabbi Samson], it is well understood why [the Gemara] could not raise any objection [from a guilt-offering]. However, regarding a burnt-offering, there is no need to be concerned about this [even] if he brings another burnt-offering, because a burnt-offering can come as a voluntary gift.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 55b:4:1.hebrew: שלא בזמנו הוי שלמים - וא"ת: כיון דמזהר זהירי בפסח, איך יבא לידי פסח שלא בזמנו? וי"ל: דלפעמים הפסח חולה ומפריש אחר, או שמא מיירי בפסח שנטמאו בעליו, אי נמי כגון שהפריש שני פסחים לאחריות, שעכשיו לא נקרב אלא אחד מהן ונשאר אחר זמנו:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 55b:4:1.english: "[A Paschal offering] not in its time is a peace-offering" - And if you say: Since they carefully guard a Paschal offering, how could it come to be a Paschal offering [offered] not in its time? And one can say: Sometimes the Paschal offering is sick and [the owner] designates another; or perhaps [the Gemara] is dealing with a Paschal offering whose owners became ritually impure; or alternatively, for example where one designated two Paschal offerings as a backup, such that now only one of them was offered, and [the other] remained after its time.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 55b:8:1.hebrew: אשתכח בת שנתה מאי - אבל לעיל גבי אשם לא מצי למיבעי "אשתכח בת שתי שנים מאי", לפי שנוכל לומר שיהיה תקנה ברעייה, דכל שבחטאת מתה — באשם רועה; ואם כן, תרעה עד שתסתאב והדמים יהיו לקייץ המזבח. אבל בחטאת אין בה תקנה כלל, ומשום הכי בעי גמרא: ומאי תקנתיה? וא"ת: לעיל דקאמר "זכרים עולות", ליחוש דילמא שעירי רגלים וראשי חדשים שהם חטאות צבור והם זכרים, וא"כ אמאי לא בעי גמרא לעיל כי הכא: "דילמא חטאות"? צ"ל דלהא ליכא למיחש, דהא לב ב"ד מתנה עליהם שאם נאבדו יהיו חולין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 55b:8:1.english: "What if it was found in its first year?" - However, earlier regarding a guilt-offering, [the Gemara] could not ask: "What if [an animal] in its second year was found?" because we could say that there would be a remedy through grazing, for [the principle is that] whatever in [the case of] a sin-offering is left to die, in [the case of] a guilt-offering grazes; and if so, it could graze until it develops a blemish, and its proceeds would go toward the "summer fruit" of the altar. Regarding a sin-offering, however, there is no remedy at all, and for that reason the Gemara asks: What is its remedy? And if you say: Earlier, where [the Master] says, "Males are burnt-offerings," let us be concerned that perhaps [the animal is one of] the he-goats of the Festivals or New Moons, which are communal sin-offerings and are male, and if so, why did the Gemara not ask earlier, just as [it asks] here: "Perhaps [they are] sin-offerings?" It must be answered that for this there is no need to be concerned, for the court has a tacit stipulation regarding them that if they are lost, they become non-sacred [chullin].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 55b:9:1.hebrew: אין לוקחין בהמה במעשר שני - פירש בקונטרס: חוץ לירושלים, משום דכתיב (דברים יד): "וצרת הכסף בידך", דהתורה הקפידה בכסף צורה; ועוד: שמא תכחש בטורח הדרך. ולא נהירא: דהא דבעינן כסף צורה, היינו דוקא דרך חילול, כגון לקנות דבר שאינו אוכל, שאז צריך לחזור ולמכור; אבל במקח, להוליך בהמה ולאוכלה בירושלים — שרי, ולא בעינא כסף צורה. והכי נמי אמר בהגוזל קמא (ב"ק דף צז:): מי שיש לו מעות בבבל שאינם יוצאין בירושלים, זבין בהמה בבבל וממטי לה בירושלים; אלמא לא בעינן כסף צורה! מיהו ללישנא ד"שמא תכחיש" לא קשה כולי האי, דאיכא למימר: דיותר טוב לקנות בהמה ולהעלותה לירושלים — ואע"ג שמתכחשת מטורח הדרך — מלהביא המעות של בבל שאינם יוצאים בירושלים; אבל ללישנא דכסף צורה קשה טובא, כדפרישית. לכך נראה לר"י לפרש, דהיינו טעמא ד"אין לוקחין בהמות כו'" — גזירה שמא יגדל עדרים עדרים. והכי נמי אמרינן בפרק לולב הגזול (סוכה דף מ:), דקאמר התם: מעות מעשר שני מתחללין על בהמה, חיה ועוף, בין חיים בין שחוטים, דברי ר' מאיר; וחכמים אומרים: על שחוטים מתחללין, על חיין אין מתחללין. ומסיק: מחלוקת בזכרים, אבל בנקבות דברי הכל אין מתחללין על חיין, שמא יגדל מהם עדרים; ובזכרים פליגי, אי גזרינן זכרים אטו נקבות אי לא, דרבי מאיר לא גזר ורבנן גזרי. והכא דקאמר "אין לוקחין" — גזירה זכרים אטו נקבות. ואם תאמר: כיון דטעמא הוי משום גזירה, אמאי קאמר התם לשון "מתחללין", דמשמע אפילו דיעבד לא מהני? והא אמר בכל דוכתי דכל דבר שהוא דרבנן בדיעבד מהני, ואם כן "מחללין" מיבעי ליה! דכוותיה אמרינן בפרק הזהב (ב"מ דף מה:), דקאמר התם: "אלא מאי דרבנן — 'אין מתחללין'? 'אין מחללין' מיבעי ליה!" ויש לומר: כיון דבההיא דלולב הגזול יש תקנה לעשות, לומר "יחזרו דמים למקומן" כדקאמר הכא, משום הכי קאמר דאפילו דיעבד לא מהני; דאי אמרינן מהני, כך לי דיעבד כמו שהיה עושה אותו בתחלה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 55b:9:1.english: One may not purchase an animal with second-tithe [money] - Rashi explained: Outside of Jerusalem, because it is written: "And you shall bind up the money in your hand" (Deuteronomy 14:25) — for the Torah was particular about [having] minted coin; and furthermore: lest it become emaciated from the wear of the journey. But this is not plausible: For that which we require minted coin applies specifically by way of deconsecration, such as purchasing something that is not food, where one then needs to sell it again; but as a purchase, to bring an animal and eat it in Jerusalem, it is permitted, and we do not require minted coin. And so too [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] Hagozel Kama (Bava Kamma 97b): One who has coins in Babylonia that do not circulate in Jerusalem may buy an animal in Babylonia and bring it to Jerusalem; evidently, we do not require minted coin! However, according to the formulation [that the reason is] "lest it become emaciated," it is not so difficult, as one could say that it is better to buy an animal and bring it up to Jerusalem — even though it will become emaciated from the wear of the journey — than to bring Babylonian coins that do not circulate in Jerusalem; but according to the formulation of minted coin, it is very difficult, as I explained. Therefore, it seems to the Ri to explain that this is the reason that "one may not purchase animals, etc.": [it is] a decree lest he raise herds upon herds [of livestock]. And so too we say in the chapter [entitled] Lulav Hagazul (Sukkah 40b), where it states there: Second-tithe money may be deconsecrated onto domesticated animals, non-domesticated animals, and birds, whether alive or slaughtered — [these are] the words of Rabbi Meir; and the Sages say: Onto slaughtered [animals] it may be deconsecrated, [but] onto live [animals] it may not be deconsecrated. And [the Gemara] concludes: [Their] dispute is with regard to males, but with regard to females, everyone agrees that it may not be deconsecrated onto live ones, lest he raise herds from them; and they disagree regarding males as to whether we decree [a prohibition against] males on account of females or not, for Rabbi Meir did not decree and the Rabbis decreed. And here, where it states "one may not purchase," [it is] a decree [forbidding] males on account of females. And if you will say: Since the reason is due to a decree, why does it state there the terminology of "are deconsecrated," which implies that even after the fact it is not effective? But behold, [the Gemara] says in all places that anything that is rabbinic is effective after the fact; and if so, it should have said "[one may not] deconsecrate"! A similar argument we say in the chapter [entitled] Hazzahav (Bava Metzia 45b), where it states there: "Rather, what [is the reason]? That it is rabbinic? [Then instead of] 'are not deconsecrated,' it should have said 'one may not deconsecrate'!" And one can say: Since in that [case in] Lulav Hagazul there is a remedy to implement — to say "the money shall return to its place," as [the baraita] says here — on that account it states that even after the fact it is not effective. For if we were to say it is effective, [people would treat it] after the fact just as if they were doing it from the outset.
